subject.title: Bug:  ignores  config and returns success on media failure

question: Should OpenClaw support a persistent outbound local-media root configuration for Feishu/shared sends, and should Feishu media upload failures hard-fail or report explicit partial success instead of returning fallback text as normal success?
rationale: The code fix is straightforward only after maintainers choose the host-file read boundary and user-visible delivery semantics for fallback text versus media failure.

options.title: Shared root contract plus explicit failure state
options.body: Add or bless a shared outbound local-media root policy, wire Feishu to it, and return hard failure or partial-success status for allowlist/upload failures.

options.title: No new persistent root config
options.body: Keep source-derived roots only, document staging/current roots clearly, and still change Feishu fallback reporting so missed media cannot look like normal success.

options.title: Preserve fallback success intentionally
options.body: Document Feishu fallback text as expected behavior and close only the unsupported config-key part after a maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Shared root contract plus explicit failure state
recommendation.body: Add or bless a shared outbound local-media root policy, wire Feishu to it, and return hard failure or partial-success status for allowlist/upload failures.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision cuts across shared outbound media access and filesystem policy, where the recent centralizing commits point most strongly.
